The post webAI Releases TwIL-8B, an 8.8B Reasoning Model Scoring 98.2 on MATH-500 appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> webAI has released TwIL-8B , an 8.8B reasoning model for math, code and instruction following. The TwIL-8B reasoning model is post-trained from IBM’s Granite 4.2 8B . Weights are on Hugging Face under a non-commercial license. webAI’s launch post frames the pitch around cost per task, not raw scale. The 4-bit build is 4.98 GiB, sized for CPU or modest-VRAM GPU inference. TL;DR Size: 8.79B parameters, dense. 131,072-token context, inherited from the base model. Runs on: CPU or modest-VRAM GPU via a 4.98 GiB Q4_K_M GGUF. Full bf16 weights are 16.38 GiB. Performance: Leads its size class on math and code, trails on knowledge benchmarks. Best: MATH-500 at 98.2, the top score in webAI’s comparison. Worst: GPQA Diamond at 70.2, 11.5 points behind Qwen3.5-9B. HLE is 12.6 (verbose variant). What is TwIL-8B? TwIL-8B is a dense decoder-only reasoning model from webAI. It has 40 layers, hidden size 4096, and 32 attention heads with 8 KV heads . Input and output are English text only. The model writes a <think> block before each answer. It ships in 2 variants with the same architecture and tokenizer. Balanced is the default and produces shorter reasoning traces. Verbose reasons longer and targets hard contest-style problems. TwIL-8B extends webAI’s TwIL family. The first members were 1.7B and 3B formal-logic models released in August 2026. How was TwIL-8B trained? webAI used 3 post-training stages : Full-parameter SFT on reasoning traces for math, STEM and instruction following. GRPO/DAPO reinforcement learning on math, code, STEM and instruction prompts. This produces the verbose variant. Length-aware RL with a reward that favors shorter traces against per-domain length references. This produces the balanced variant. Training pools were decontaminated with 13-gram matching against AIME, HMMT, MATH-500, GPQA and other evals. How does TwIL-8B perform on benchmarks? All TwIL-8B scores are self-reported, high-effort pass@1 with thinking enabled. Scores marked † were measured on the verbose variant only. Math : TwIL-8B scores 98.2 on MATH-500. Qwen3.5-9B lists 96.6 on a third-party leaderboard . Gemma 4 31B scored 87.9 in Red Hat’s lighteval run . On AIME 2025, TwIL-8B posts 88.3 against 87.1 for Gemma 4 31B. On AIME 2026 it scores 88.3, behind Qwen3.5-9B at 92.5 and Gemma 4 31B at 89.2 . Code : LiveCodeBench† is 81.6, against 65.6 for Qwen3.5-9B and 80.0 for Gemma 4 31B. webAI notes its LiveCodeBench version was not recorded. Competitor scores are v6. Instruction following : IFBench† is 74.4, 9.9 points above Qwen3.5-9B at 64.5. IFEval is level, at 91.8 vs 91.5. Knowledge : This is the weak spot. GPQA Diamond is 70.2, against 81.7 for Qwen3.5-9B and 84.3 for Gemma 4 31B. MMLU-Pro† is 76.5 vs 82.5 for Qwen3.5-9B. Across 13 shared benchmarks, TwIL-8B goes 7-6 against Qwen3.5-9B. Against Gemma 4 31B, about 3.5x its size, it goes 3-11. Does TwIL-8B use fewer reasoning tokens? Yes, against its closest open peer. On AIME 2026, TwIL-8B averages about 19.5k output tokens per problem. Qwen3.5-9B uses 31.2k, so TwIL-8B uses 38% fewer. It scores 4.2 points lower. On HMMT Feb 2026 the gap is 32.9k vs 40.6k, or 19% fewer. Frontier models remain far leaner. webAI cites about 5k tokens per AIME 2026 problem for GPT-5.5. webAI states that harnesses and tokenizers differ, so treat this as directional. All scores self-reported by each vendor unless marked. How do you run TwIL-8B locally? from_pretrained("webAI-Official/TwIL-8B") loads the balanced variant. Pass subfolder="verbose" for the verbose one. The model card lists GGUF builds for llama.cpp: Q4_K_M, 4.98 GiB, for both variants Q8_0, 8.70 GiB, verbose only F16, 16.38 GiB, verbose only Give it a large generation budget. The card’s example sets max_new_tokens=32768 . A short budget truncates reasoning and scores far worse. All reported scores used bf16 weights, so expect small drops at Q4_K_M. No hosted inference provider serves the model on Hugging Face yet. Key Takeaways TwIL-8B is an 8.79B dense reasoning model post-trained from IBM Granite 4.2 8B. It posts 98.2 on MATH-500 and 81.6† on LiveCodeBench. It uses 38% fewer tokens than Qwen3.5-9B on AIME 2026. Knowledge is weak: GPQA Diamond trails Qwen3.5-9B by 11.5 points. Weights are open but licensed for non-commercial use only. Check out the model card and weights on Hugging Face and webAI’s announcement on X . The post Ricursive AI Releases Ripple-65B Preview: A 65B Dense Open-Weight Model Scoring 80.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Ricursive Intelligence just released Ripple-65B Preview . Ripple-65B Preview is a 65B dense open-weight model from Ricursive, pretrained from scratch for agentic coding. It is a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model behind Ricursive’s AI chip design platform. The main claim: 80.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 , the top self-reported score among US open-weight models. Every MoE rival it beats on that test carries 501B to 975B total parameters. TL;DR Size: 65B dense (65B active), pretrained on 12T tokens, up to 1M context. Runs on: BF16 on datacenter GPUs (250 tok/s on 2x B200). Experimental NVFP4 build targets NVIDIA DGX Spark. Performance: Frontier-level agentic coding for its size; trails larger MoE models on knowledge and science coding. Best: Terminal-Bench 2.1, 80.5 (self-reported).
